svg.title: core.py architecture
svg.desc: Diagram showing the six layers of core.py: MILPProblem, LP relaxation, PrincipledMWUA, StructuralFeatureEngine, GraphState, and reductions
svg.text: builds the world model that branching.py navigates

g.text: Generic container: minimise c·x subject to A_ub·x ≤ b_ub, A_eq·x = b_eq, x ∈ {0,1}.
build_mvc_problem() converts a graph into a vertex cover ILP (edges rewritten as ≤ constraints).
Solves continuous relaxation (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) at every node to get lower bounds and fractional values.
Provides pruning power and branching uncertainty. Augmented by structure — not replaced.
Layer 3 — PrincipledMWUA (conceptual heart of the dissertation)
Computes ONE root-level structural snapshot. Avoids repeated expensive global analysis.

svg.text: Iterate until delta = mean|x_avg_now − x_avg_prev| is small (structure stabilised).

g.text: 0 = ambiguous · 0.5 = very stable. Reused throughout DFS.
Wraps MWUA into clean VertexFeatures: mwua_x_avg, mwua_certainty, root_lp_certainty.
Intentionally lightweight — no embeddings, no GNNs, no repeated recomputation.
Tracks residual structure incrementally as DFS fixes variables. Updated per node, not from scratch.
If LP returns x_i = 0 or x_i = 1 exactly, those assignments are safe to fix immediately.
Combined with isolated-vertex and pendant reductions to shrink residual search space.
Only reduces when LP certainty and graph structure agree — never trusts one signal alone.
